label: paragraph_title
text: SHEER HUMBUG

label: text
text: CAUSTIC COMMENT ON BUDGET SPEECH

label: text
text: PROFLIGATU AND BANKRUPT.

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: London, April 26.

label: text
text: In the House of Commons to-day Opposition Day in connection with the Budget was fully taken advantage of by Mr. P. Snowden in accusing Mr. Winston Churchill of increasing national expenditure by £30,000,000 in 18 months and making an outrageous settlement with Italy simply in order to get £4,000,000 to include

label: vision_footnote
text: Y " Mr. Winston Churchill.

label: text
text: in the present Budget. The Government was undoubtedly in the grip of the banks and financial houses, whilst Mr. Churchill's statement regarding the silk duties was sheer humbug.

label: text
text: The ex-Chancellor (Mr. Philip Snowden) scathingly criticised the betting tax, which he alleged was an outrage on the most sacred feelings of a vast number of people and would lead to collusion between backers and book-

label: vision_footnote
text: Mr. Phillip Snowden

label: text
text: makers. He recalled that he described last year's Budget as the "rich man's Budget." This year it was the Budget of the profile and bankrupt." (Loud Labour cheers).

label: paragraph_title
text: Mild Liberal

label: text
text: Sir J. Simon (Liberal, Spen Valley) was milder in his criticism. He thought that betting could be regarded as an imprimatur form of excitement which caused havoc to homes when indulged in excessively. Moreover, the tax would encourage illegal forms of betting.

label: vision_footnote
text: Sir J. Simon.

label: text
text: Sir J. Simon, warmly repudiated the Chancellor's competence regarding 10 years' guarantee of Imperial Preference.

label: text
text:
Conservatives Divided.
London, April 27.

label: text
text: The betting tax promises to be the controversial feature of the Budget. It is opposed by the churches and bookmakers from different angles, whilst the Conservatives are divided—one section opposing the tax on moral grounds and another demanding legalisation against betting.

label: text
text: Prominent racing men and bookmakers at Newmarket are doubtful as regards the yield of the tax and predict that it will be almost unworkable.

label: text
text: The director of a big London-firm of commission agents said that the backer cannot afford to pay the tax, which would mean that the betting public are losing three as much as at present estimated. The bookmakers will have to increase their staff by 50 per cent.

label: text
text: Lord Lonsdale expressed the opinion that the scheme cannot satisfactorily be completed unless EFFECTS OF NEW TREATY.

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: London, April 27.

label: text
text: The general impression of the Germano-Soviet Treaty in official circles in London is that many phrases are vague, indefinite, and capable of another interpretation. There does not appear at first sight to be anything objectionable.

label: text
text: The newspapers agree that the Treaty does not create a new situation and that the general lines of German foreign policy are unchanged, which fact is regretted by some of the more violent Nationalist journals.

label: text
text:
Somma che League.
Paris Anvill 276

label: text
text: The “Homme Libre” argues that the Soviet will thus enter the League in Germany's baggage, as once Germany is a member of the League she will be unable to associate herself with any League decision without being sure of agreeing with Moscow.

label: text
text: The paper concludes that the Soviet thus joins the League without any commitments or responsibilities.

label: text
text: Concern Not Dispelled.

label: text
text: An active exchange of views is proceeding between London and Paris, but it is premature to talk of representations being made to Berlin.

label: text
text: The publication of the text of the Russo-German Treaty has not dispelled the concern in French political circles in regard to its possible "effects on" the fabric of Geneva and Locarno.

label: text
text: The "Temps" says that Germany wants to reserve the option to choose between the Western Powers and Soviet Russia when the fateful hour strikes, but it is hardly conceivable that such an attitude can be compatible with Germany's unconditional entry to the League of Nations.

label: text
text: RODUCTION GREATEST FOR OVER A YEAR.

label: paragraph_title
text: U.S. INDUSTRIES.

label: text
text: ACTIVITY IN MILLIS

label: text
text: (Reuter's American Service.)

label: text
text: The Federal Reserve Board's monthly index of production in the basic industries shows that the increases in March reached the highest level for more than a year. The increases were marked in "steel" ingots, pig iron, anthracite coal, copper, and news-print.

label: text
text: There was also great activity in textile mills, and the output of motor cars was the largest since October.

label: text
text: BRITAIN'S IDLE LIST CREATES A RECORD.

label: paragraph_title
text: BELOW A MILLION.

label: text
text: The total of unemployed persons on Monday last recorded in the Labour Exchanges of Great Britain was 997,000.

label: text
text: This is the first time for several years that the figures have dropped below a million.

BRITISH ASSURANCES.

label: text
text: (Router's American Service.)

label: text
text: Washington, April 27.

label: text
text:
Nineteen minutes debate sufficed for the Senate to approve of the Latvian debt settlement.
The Senate also approved of the debt agreements with Esthonia and Roumania.

label: text
text: Senator Reed, the chief spokesman of the Opposition, declared that most probably Latvia would again become a part of Russia long before the 62 years laid down in the settlement had passed.

label: text
text: Senator Reed predicted that Great Britain would make the Italian debt settlement the basis of a demand for a revision of the British debt agreement.

label: text
text: Senator Smoot replied that Great Britain had given assurances that she would not object to any settlement which the United States might make with other nations.

label: paragraph_title
text: RUSSIAN FLOODS.

label: text
text: SEVERAL VILLAGES UNDER WATER.

label: text
text: EIGHT LIVES: LOST:

label: text
text: (Router's Service.)

label: text
text: Moscow, April 27.

label: text
text:
The Volga and its upper tribu-
tinies have overflowed their banks.

label: text
text: The River Klazma has flooded the town of Orekhovo 45 miles east of Moscow.

label: text
text: Eight persons were drowned. Eleven bridges were destroyed. Many textile mills are idle. Loss of life is also reported at Rybinsk where the Volga is 50 feet

label: text
text: Scores of villages are flooded. The inhabitants have taken refuge on the roofs.

label: text
text: Detachments of the Red Army are blowing up ice jams on the rivers in order that the waters can flow to their natural course

label: text
text: AND POOR MUSSOLINI REMAINS!

label: text
text: In torrential rain, more than 50,000 Fascists assembled in the Cathedral Square last night to pay homage to Signor Mussolini, who received a most enthusiastic ovation. Mussolini appeared on a balcony surrounded by the local notables

label: text
text: Referring to the downpour he remarked: "I believe you would stand with the same impassivity under fire," and concluded with "Bullets pass; O Blackshirts and Mussolini remains." This was received with deafening cheers.

label: paragraph_title
text: SOVIET FINANCE.

label: text
text:
REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE
GREATER

label: text
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text:
Moscow, April 27.
The Soviet Central Executive Committee concluded the fortnight's session by unanimously adopting a resolution on Military-Innoff's report fully approving the Government's foreign policy. They also adopted a law reforming agricultural taxation, and the ratification of the Soviet budget which showed estimated revenue 4,809,000,000 roubles, being an increase of 37,000 compared with the original estimates, and estimated expenditure 8,922,000,000 roubles being an increase of 20,000.
(Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: After several days' intensive conferences, in which the Prime Minister was most active, the mine owners intimated their willingness to participate in an open tri-party meeting at which they would not impose any limitation regarding the scope of the discussion.

label: text
text: Thereafter an hour's meeting of the three parties was held in the House of Commons, and adjourned till to-morrow.

label: doc_title
text: 1916 MASSACRE.

label: text
text: AMERICA NOT ENTITLED TO DAMAGES

label: text
text: (Reuter's American Service.)

label: text
text: The neutral Chairman of the Mexican delegates on the American Claims Commission has signed and issued their decision to the effect that the United States is not entitled to damages for the massacre of Americans at Santay Safe, Mexico, in 1916.

label: text
text: The American delegate declared the decision was illegal and did not bind the United States.

label: paragraph_title

label: text
text: TROUBLE OF AN AMERICAN RAILWAY.

label: text
text: (Router's Service.)

label: text
text: Chicago, April 27.

label: text
text: Judge Wilkerson, of the Federal Court has ordered the foreclosure of the sale of the Chicago-Milwaukee-St. Paul Railway, whose affairs are already in the hands of a receiver.

label: paragraph_title
text: RESCUERS · DROWNED.

label: paragraph_title
text: Tokyo, April 20.

label: text
text: Of 27 fishermen, who attempted to rescue a vessel in "distress" off Hakodate, Hokkaido, thirteen were drowned owing to the capsizing of their junks, whereas the crew on board, the wrecked vessel were cast ashore and saved. "Eastern News Agency."

label: text
text: SINO-AMERICAN PACT NOT

label: text
text: Washington has replied to the Chinese Government, expressing disapproval of the latter's proposal for the revision of the Sino-American Agreement.—Eastern

label: paragraph_title
text: AIR CRASH.

label: text
text:
TWO CHILDREN KILLED IN
NACASAART

label: text
text: Owing to a gust of wind an aeroplane landing at Oil in Nara prefecture fell at an altitude of 10 metres, on a number of school children who were watching the landing. Two were killed and several seriously injured. The pilot was not hurt but the machine was badly damaged. — Reuter.

STOLEN GOODS
SOLICITOR'S RINGS FOUND
IN PAWN
TWO MEN CHARGED

label: text
text:
Theft of a diamond ring and a ruby ring set in platinum, the property of Mr. C. A. S. Russ, was one of many charges preferred against two Chinese at the Central Magistracy this morning.
The first accused, defended by Mr. A. E. Hall, pleaded not guilty. The other only admitted a charge of giving a false name and address when pledging clothing at pawn-shops.

label: text
text:
Giving evidence from the witness box, Mr. Russ said that the rings were left by his wife on a shelf at a tailor's shop in D'Aguilar Street at 5:30 one afternoon and she forgot all about them until 8 p.m. when he heard of it while away at Fanling. On returning the next morning he carried out investigations at the shop, but without result. Referring to compensation to the pawn-broker in respect of the diamond ring which had been pledged for $50 and for which he originally paid £280, Mr. Russ strongly opposed any payment, stating that the article was traced owing to the ticket being found.
His Worship described the charges as serious in adjourning

label: text
text: Prosecuting in a case of theft of copper plates from the Hongkong Electric Company, Mr. L. R. Andrewes pressed for severe punishment against a Chinese, as he said that thefts of this nature were continually taking place without being detected.

label: text
text: Accused, pleading guilty was sentenced to one month's hard labour.
